I was playing a recently-released game that had raised funds via Kickstarter. Not too far into the game, it became quite apparent that it has a heavily Christian message to it which put me off, as I don't want to be evanglised to or play a character in a game that will essentially go out spreading the "gospel".

There's no mention of religion anywhere on the Kickstarter page (that I could find). It's not really a huge deal but it feels...dishonest. I didn't back the game but if I had, I'd have been most upset that the money had been used for a game with a not-so-subtle Christian message; I feel it's something that ought to have been noted on the Kickstarter page and now on its Steam store page.

What do you guys think about this? The part I'm referring to in the game is at the beginning of Chapter 2. You can see this in the first 6 minutes of this let's play: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I9BOU43gyqQ Drinking from the rushlight is synonymous with accepting Jesus into your heart. I stopped playing after this but the entire game is centred on curing The Vague, so infer what you will from that.

Maybe I'm over-reacting, and I don't want to cause problems for the guys who made the game, but it's something I personally would have taken issue with as a backer on Kickstarter.

From a game-player standpoint, it's only a game.

Most games these days are more like interactive movies and those movies have to have a story. The creators of this game built a world and then a lore to function within that world. There are plenty more games like this that have something similar, I'm sure, however, the thing to remember is if you didn't enjoy playing it, then you stopped and that's fine. If you didn't back it financially, then you've lost no money there.

Honestly, I don't really see anything but some similarities which I'll concede are pretty striking, however, I wouldn't bother with it.

My basis for not bothering with the game in the first place is that the dialogue is terrible and the graphics and controls seem clunky.
